newsitem.title: UK: Melrose unit to buy into Siberian oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Melrose unit to buy into Siberian oil deal.

text.p: Melrose Energy said on Thursday it was establishing a new company called Newco, 49 percent owned by Melrose, through which it was buying an indirect 10 percent stake for 19.69 million stg in a western Siberian oil venture.
The venture to buy an interest in Evikhon Oil Joint Stock Company is to develop about 1.25 billion barrels of recoverable oil reserves as well as "certain other interests".
The vendor is placing 24.1 million new shares at 48 pence per share to raise 11.57 million stg.
Newco's indirect stake in Evikhon will be 20 percent.
Total recoverable reserves attributable to Newco's indirect investments are about 175 million barrels of oil and those attributable to Melrose are about 86 million barrels.

Institutional and other investors, including some Melrose directors, have invested about 7.25 million stg in Newco. Melrose said in wanted to lost Newco on the Alternative Investment Market "as soon as possible".
"This transaction is Melrose's first in Russia," said Melrose chief executive Henry Cameron, adding that the oil field was forecast to reach a production level of 120,000 barrels per day by 2002.
"We are optimistic that Newco will become in its own right an important vehicle for future investment in Russian oil and gas," he added.
